title: Flame spread across composite fabrics
subtitle: Concurrent flow · SIBAL fabric
author: James S. T’ien and collaborators
summary: 27 fabric tests connect oxygen concentration and changing ventilation with flame growth, quenching, and ignition observations. Table 7.1 records the starting and ending airflow for each test.
insight: The report describes slower steady spread at lower airflow, lower oxygen levels, and narrower sample widths within these tests.
limitations: Two oxygen readings carry an author warning.
Eight samples are explicitly marked as reused.
Flow endpoints do not describe the complete time history.

title: Extinction limits in thin PMMA films
subtitle: Opposed flow · Thin films
author: Subrata Bhattacharjee and collaborators
summary: Thin-film experiments examine opposed-flow flame spread and extinction while changing oxygen, sample thickness, and ventilation. The imported table contains 22 tests assigned to this research group.
insight: Use this section to investigate low-flow extinction and the role of thin-sample geometry. Detailed spread rates require the report’s figures or run-level analysis.
limitations: Many air-display cells contain a sequence of settings.
Time-resolved spread rates are not extracted in this version.
Sample descriptions vary in their level of detail.

title: Flame spread over thicker PMMA slabs
subtitle: Opposed flow · 1–5 mm slabs
author: Fletcher J. Miller, Indrek Wichman and collaborators
summary: 20 tests study one- and two-sided burning of PMMA slabs, with thicknesses from 1 to 5 mm. The report describes adjusting the opposed airflow as each test progresses.
insight: Section 5 connects sample thickness, oxygen, and flow with flame-spread analysis. Its reported airflow range is 3–20 cm/s; the imported display strings need phase-by-phase interpretation.
limitations: Variable-flow records cannot be reduced to one speed.
Pressure is not a run-level field in the imported table.
Flame-spread values still need figure or video extraction.

title: Opposed flame spread along PMMA rods
subtitle: Opposed flow · Clear and black rods
author: Carlos Fernandez-Pello and collaborators
summary: Rod experiments examine opposed flame spread across sample sizes and oxygen levels. The experimental table preserves fan settings, air-display notes, and before/after gas readings for 27 tests.
insight: Rod diameter, flow direction, and material form matter when selecting comparable evidence. Keep these records separate from film and slab experiments.
limitations: Several display values contain qualitative notes.
Two final oxygen readings are flagged for review.
This subset has no imported detector-performance measurements.

title: PMMA flammability in stagnation flow
subtitle: Axial stagnation flow · PMMA rods
author: Sandra L. Olson and collaborators
summary: Axial stagnation-flow research studies PMMA rod flammability as ventilation, rod radius, and oxygen change. The imported table contains 27 test records for this group.
insight: The report examines both low-flow quenching and blowoff. Its hardware discussion also explains the air probe’s response time and limited low-speed resolution.
limitations: A zero air-display reading is not proof of zero flow.
Some CO readings are over-range codes.
Fan settings require the corresponding calibration.

title: Ignition observations for Nomex barriers
subtitle: Material screening · Nomex III
author: Paul V. Ferkul
summary: Three Nomex samples were evaluated because the material is used as an ISS fire barrier. The report states that these samples did not ignite under their tested conditions.
insight: These are three specific observations, not a universal nonflammability certification. Other atmospheres, specimen configurations, and ignition conditions require their own evidence.
limitations: Only three Nomex tests are in this subset.
No extrapolation to oxygen-enriched habitats is established.
A separate wax-candle test is excluded from this group.
